title_en: MacroVoices #551 Michael Every: Decoding The Global Geopolitical Puzzle
title_zh: Michael Every：解码全球地缘政治迷局
subtitle_zh: Rabobank 全球策略师剖析伊朗、俄乌、格陵兰与柴油危机背后的多方博弈
description: MacroVoices #551 Michael Every: Decoding The Global Geopolitical Puzzle

turns.en: The joke at the moment is if you're an interest rate trader or an FX trader at the moment, you have to be an oil trader. You've got to look at that to understand what bond deals are going to do.
turns.zh: 现在圈子里有个玩笑：如果你眼下是利率交易员或者外汇交易员，你就得同时是原油交易员。你得盯油，才能搞清楚债券收益率接下来会怎么走。

turns.en: That was Michael Everry. I'm Eric Townsend. This is Macro Voices and boy, this episode's going to be a doozy. We're going to talk about the entire world of geopolitics all the way from what's going on with Iran to what just happened with this escalation and the Ukraine conflict and the strikes on the Russian diesel refineries and what happens if we have a diesel crisis, diesel exports from the United States, China, Greenland, Denmark, stablecoins and much more.
turns.zh: 刚才那段是 Michael Every。我是 Eric Townsend，这里是 Macro Voices。伙计，这期节目可太有料了。我们要聊整个地缘政治格局，从伊朗局势，到乌克兰冲突刚刚升级、俄罗斯柴油炼厂遭袭，一旦出现柴油危机怎么办，美国的柴油出口，中国、格陵兰、丹麦、稳定币等等，都会谈到。

turns.en: So put your seatbelt on and stay tuned at the end of this interview for a special announcement that you're really going to love because we've been listening to listener feedback and we're going to do a format change to make sure you get a double dose of Michael Everry this week on Macro Voices.
turns.zh: 所以请系好安全带，一直听到这期访谈最后，有一个特别公告，你肯定会喜欢，因为我们一直在听大家的反馈，我们要做一次节目形式的调整，让你在这一周的 Macro Voices 里听到双份的 Michael Every。

turns.en: Let's dive straight into this interview. Joining me now is Michael Everry, global strategist in economics and markets for Rabobank or Rabobank or something like that depends on which language you're speaking.
turns.zh: 我们直接进入今天的访谈。现在加入我们的是 Michael Every，Rabobank 的全球策略师，负责经济和市场研究——或者叫 Rabobank，具体怎么念取决于你说的是哪种语言。

turns.en: Michael, it's great to get you back. Boy, geopolitics is your specialty. There's no shortage of that. So let's dive in. The Iran conflict is probably first on people's minds, something that is surprising to me in the news flow and just other people I talked to, seems so clear to me that a major escalation campaign, you started with Trump saying that he was making threats, then Iran says we're not going to escalate symmetrically anymore, and then you see East West Pipeline, then
turns.zh: Michael，非常高兴请你回来。伙计，地缘政治是你的强项，现在这方面话题可太多了。我们直接开始吧。伊朗冲突可能是大家最关心的，让我很意外的是，从新闻和其他人的讨论来看，一场大规模升级行动好像已经很清楚了：一开始是 Trump 放话威胁，然后伊朗说我们不会再对等升级了，接着你就看到 East-West Pipeline（东西输油管），然后

turns.en: you see Yanbu, then you see Bob Elmandeb, wait a minute, when the first airplane hit the World Trade Center, you weren't sure what happened.
turns.zh: 你看到 Yanbu，然后看到 Bab el-Mandeb（曼德海峡）。等一下，当第一架飞机撞上世贸中心的时候，你还搞不清楚发生了什么。

turns.en: When the second one hit, the question was, how many more planes are coming? So it seems to me like we're beginning a big escalation, but oil straight down because of why again, because it's like 38th time that we're declaring victory.
turns.zh: 当第二架撞上去的时候，问题就变成了：还有多少架飞机在飞过来？所以在我看来，一场大规模升级正在开始，可是油价却直线下挫，为什么？因为这已经是我们第 38 次宣告胜利了。

turns.en: I'm not buying it. What do you think? The movement in oil in the last day in a bit has a couple of different drivers, but I think hope, which is not justified by the reality around us is one of them yet again.
turns.zh: 我可不买账。你怎么看？过去一天多油价的走势有几个不同的驱动因素，但我认为其中一个还是希望——一种被我们周围的现实反复证伪的希望。

turns.en: To add my two cents' worth to what you just said, I'd argued that when you looked at the economic blockade that the US was imposing on Iran, finally, after having experimented with other formats, if it worked, Iran's incentive would be to escalate militarily elsewhere.
turns.zh: 在你刚才说的基础上我补两句。我的看法是，当你审视美国对伊朗实施的经济封锁——在尝试了其他各种形式之后终于上了这一招——如果这封锁奏效，那伊朗的动机就是要在别处以军事方式升级。

turns.en: And that's exactly what you're seeing, whether it's either direct or whether it's via proxies with an element of deniability, but we all know who is really behind it.
turns.zh: 而现在你看到的正是这种情况，不管是直接出手，还是通过代理人、带一点可否认性，但我们都知道真正幕后的势力是谁。

turns.en: And boy, has it worked. If you see the kafafal around the Red Sea, the Houthis in Yemen, that East West Pipeline, Yambu, et cetera, et cetera, oil was up to 110 bucks spent for a while on the back of that.
turns.zh: 而且效果显著。你看看红海一带的动静，也门的 Houthis（胡塞武装），那条 East-West Pipeline，Yanbu 等等，油价一度飙到每桶 110 美元。

turns.en: But I think the really important point is what you just made clear, that we now have a situation where Yambu can be attacked all the time, Riyadh can be attacked all the time, Aramco can be attacked all the time, and that East West Pipeline, having already been here, is imminently hit a bull.
turns.zh: 但我认为真正关键的一点是你刚才讲清楚的那件事：我们现在处在这样一种局面——Yanbu 可以不断被袭击，Riyadh 可以不断被袭击，Aramco（沙特阿美）可以不断被袭击，而那条已经中过招的 East-West Pipeline，随时可能再次被击中。

turns.en: What makes anyone think that can't be repeated again and again and again? So unless we are now pricing for peace in our time, which is as true in the Middle East as it is in Russia with Ukraine, unless you have discreet and distinct knowledge of when these wars will end, you are just hoping if you're going to try to start to price in the fact that everything is going to get better.
turns.zh: 凭什么说这种事情不会一而再、再而三地重演？所以，除非我们现在就在为「我们这代人的和平」（peace in our time）定价——而这种说法在中东和在俄罗斯对乌克兰的战争里同样不成立——除非你对这些战争何时结束有确切、独到的情报，否则你想开始为「一切都会好转」定价，那就只是在抱有希望而已。

turns.en: Now we recorded this interview before markets up on Wednesday, so day and a half or so before our listeners will hear it. The latest thing from the Trump administration was, look, it's pretty darn clear after meeting with Iran that they're going to agree to a peace agreement right after the US election, because it would be foolish of them not to and it only makes sense.
turns.zh: 我们录制这次访谈是在周三市场开盘之前，也就是听众听到节目的一天半之前。Trump 政府最新的说法是：跟伊朗会谈之后已经非常清楚了，他们会在美国大选之后马上同意达成和平协议，因为不同意才是傻，这才符合逻辑。

turns.en: I'm missing the logic, Michael. It apparently makes sense after the US election, but not before it. Help me with the math here. I think what we are seeing there is that the American administration is finally starting to understand how to mirror the Iranians in the absolute BS that they come out with internationally, because that doesn't make any sense whatsoever.
turns.zh: Michael，我没看懂这个逻辑。大选之后说得通，但大选之前就不行？你帮我把这里的数学捋清楚。我觉得我们看到的是，美国政府终于开始学会用伊朗人那套满嘴跑火车的方式去回敬伊朗人，因为那个说法本身根本讲不通。

turns.en: Our view or my view specifically has been the complete opposite, that once the election is out of the way, if Trump's won, fantastic, if Trump's lost, well then he still has to escalate anyway, whether it's by our executive orders at home or military action abroad.
turns.zh: 我们的观点，或者更准确地说我个人的观点，恰恰相反：一旦大选尘埃落定，如果 Trump 赢了，很好；如果 Trump 输了，他也还是得升级，要么在国内用行政命令，要么在国外动武。

turns.en: That is our base case, that you will see escalation once the election is out of the way. Of course, if Iran escalates more in the interim, you can see the US have to strike back even before then.
turns.zh: 这就是我们的基准情形——大选结束之后你会看到升级。当然，如果伊朗在这中间升级得更厉害，美国可能等不到大选之后就得动手还击。

turns.en: If diesel prices are going to be where they are right now, you could even argue that the distraction of saying, well, at least we're bombing them might play better with some voters than saying we're doing nothing, but we promise you there'll be a peace deal like five weeks from now when you've just been suffering at the Bowser for the past five weeks.
turns.zh: 如果柴油价格维持在现在的水平，你甚至可以说，「至少我们在轰炸他们」这种转移视线的说法，对一部分选民来说可能比「我们什么都没做，但我们保证五周之后就能达成和平协议」更受用——尤其是过去五周他们一直在加油站被油价折磨。

turns.en: It doesn't make any sense. It isn't what we expect. It doesn't mean that there's zero possibility of suddenly some miraculous deal being struck, but if you look what the starting position and what the finishing position of both the US and Iran are, we are still where we were in the very early days of this, which is saying that they're two irreconcilable positions and that that blockade is working well for
turns.zh: 这讲不通。这不是我们的预期。也不排除突然之间奇迹般达成某种协议的可能性，但如果看美国和伊朗双方的起始立场和终局立场，我们还是在这件事最早期的位置，也就是：双方立场不可调和，而封锁对美国

turns.en: the US. I'm sure you are as cognizant as I am that in the background, we have lots and lots of wheels turning to make sure that if and when we get a US escalation, it's going to have a lot more people attacking alongside it.
turns.zh: 很有利。我相信你也和我一样清楚：在幕后，大量的机器正在转动，为的是确保一旦美国真的升级，会有一大堆人跟着一起上。

turns.en: It won't just be the US. It's more likely to be the US and Israel and a coalition from the GCC to try and really finish the job. So that's what I expect instead.
turns.zh: 不会只有美国单打独斗，更可能是美国加上以色列，再加上海合会（GCC）的一个联盟，真正想把事情做个了断。所以我预期的反而是这个。

turns.en: It seems to me, Michael, that if you are any of President Trump's enemies around the world, whether that's Iran, whether that's Putin in Russia, anyone who is not wanting President Trump to stay in power, you have an incredibly strong incentive to do everything possible to keep oil prices elevated through the US election.
turns.zh: Michael，在我看来，如果你是 Trump 总统在世界上任何一个对手——不管是伊朗，是俄罗斯的 Putin，还是任何不希望 Trump 继续掌权的人——你都有极强的动机，想尽一切办法在美国大选之前把油价维持在高位。

turns.en: Because if you can somehow cause the US election to not go in Trump's favor to the point that the Republicans lose both houses of Congress, then it's very likely that most of what Trump wants to do next is probably going to be interrupted by yet another impeachment trial and so forth.
turns.zh: 因为如果你能以某种方式让美国大选的结果不利于 Trump，让共和党丢掉国会的两院，那么 Trump 接下来想干的很多事情，很可能就会被又一场弹劾审判之类的东西打断。

turns.en: So am I right to think that there's a lot of people, obviously people who are Trump's allies would have the opposite, but it seems to me like there's a lot of motivation around the world to escalate and make this worse through the US election?
turns.zh: 所以我想的是不是这样：世界上有很多人——当然，Trump 的盟友会有相反的动机——但看起来在美国大选期间，有很多动机促使局势升级、把事情搞得更糟？

turns.en: Yeah, I agree completely. And that's something one needs to be cognizant of at all times. All I will throw in on top of that is something which is an adjunct to it, that it's very important to consider, that we have in the past spoken on this issue and I've said that obviously Trump went into Iran hoping it would be like Venezuela, which it wasn't, which has been in geopolitical terms and oil terms a fantastic success, let's be clear.
turns.zh: 对，我完全同意，这一点必须时时刻刻记在心里。我再补充一个相关的观察：我们过去讨论过这个话题，我说过，Trump 显然是一开始抱着「伊朗会变成第二个委内瑞拉」的希望进去的，结果并非如此——而委内瑞拉从地缘政治和石油的角度来看，我们要说清楚，那是一场巨大的成功。

turns.en: So he was hoping to replicate that, but I said to you that if that were not possible, it isn't necessarily the disaster that it looks for him.
turns.zh: 所以他本来是想复制那一套的。但我跟你说过，如果复制不了，这对他来说也不一定就是看上去那样的灾难。

turns.en: And I'm including that even within the context of what you just said, which is correct that it's painful for the US, it's painful for him politically.
turns.zh: 而且我说这话的时候，已经把你刚才讲的那层考虑进去了——就是这对美国是痛苦的，对他在政治上也是痛苦的。

turns.en: Because if you look at the US ink rather than just the current occupant of the White House and if you look at global energy as a strategic asset rather than a market where you buy and sell and trade, whose energy production and refineries in their totality would you want to hold if you're an alien looking down from outer space about to invade the earth?
turns.zh: 因为如果你看的不是白宫当前的这位入住者，而是美国这盘大棋；如果你把全球能源当成一项战略资产，而不是一个买卖交易的市场——假设你是一个从太空俯视地球、准备入侵的外星人，你会想拥有哪个国家的全部能源生产和炼厂？

turns.en: Well, it would be the Americas plural and it would be the Middle East. And I'm sure you have those numbers, those data, immediately to mind when you're thinking about that.
turns.zh: 答案是美洲（复数）加上中东。我相信你脑子里立刻就能浮现出相关的数据。

turns.en: It's nobody else. Everyone else is important in different areas, but they're not the whole story. So if Trump goes into the Middle East and can manage to defeat Iran as we've spoken about before, which is why I think he will escalate with others, then he's got both of those in hand and that gives him a fantastic amount of leverage over everybody else, China and others.
turns.zh: 没有别人。其他地区在各自领域都很重要，但它们不是全局。所以如果 Trump 进入中东，能够像我们之前讨论过的那样把伊朗压下去——这也是我认为他会拉上其他人一起升级的原因——那他手上就同时握住了这两块，这就给了他极大的杠杆去对付其他人，包括中国等等。

turns.en: But, and here's the real takeaway. I know Anas al-Haji has said similar things from very early on and I was always open to the idea. If he goes in and he can't manage to topple Iran rather than retreating and saying, oh, dear, energy prices are high, right, okay, here are the keys to the Middle East.
turns.zh: 但——这才是真正的重点——我知道 Anas Alhajji 很早就说过类似的话，我一直也持开放态度：如果他进去之后没法把伊朗推翻，与其退回来喊「哎呀，能源价格太高了，好吧，这是中东的钥匙，交给你了」，

turns.en: All that energy block now shifts towards China, towards Russia, towards North Korea, towards Iran, et cetera, et cetera. You just keep at it one way or another.
turns.zh: 那整块能源版图就会转向中国、俄罗斯、朝鲜、伊朗等等，你就得用另一种方式坚持下去。

turns.en: You ensure that one way or another the Middle East remains destabilized, which isn't hard to do because there are a lot of people who are very keen on destabilizing it.
turns.zh: 你要用各种办法确保中东持续处于动荡——这不难做到，因为有很多人非常热衷于让它动荡。

turns.en: And at that point, the collective energy in the Americas still look really, really good from outer space and you still have, in relative terms, a very strong hand and leverage against others, even if in nominal terms and in electoral terms, coming up to the midterms, you suffer.
turns.zh: 到那时候，从太空看下来，整个美洲的能源资产依然极其漂亮，你在相对意义上仍然握有一手很强的牌，仍然对其他人有杠杆，即便从名义上和选举角度、临近中期选举时你要吃点苦头。

turns.en: Is there a risk that if this does not go the president's way and we get to the point where the election is rapidly approaching and it seems like there's just no way to get the cost of energy prices back down?
turns.zh: 有没有这样一种风险：如果事情没有朝总统希望的方向发展，选举又快速逼近，能源价格看起来根本压不下来，

turns.en: Is that then the opening where the Trump administration throws the Hail Mary pass to say, okay, we're going to massively escalate and send the message to the voters that, okay, he really did end it this time.
turns.zh: 那会不会就是 Trump 政府扔出「孤注一掷」（Hail Mary）传球的机会？告诉选民：好，我们要大规模升级，让他这一次真的把这事做个了断。

turns.en: He did the big thing and we had the gigantic escalation militarily that both reignited some patriotism among the American people to support the president and also created maybe a better claim he could make that he finished it.
turns.zh: 他做了这件大事，来了一次规模巨大的军事升级，既重新点燃了美国民众支持总统的爱国情绪，也让他更有底气宣称「是我结束了这场战争」。

turns.en: I would not rule that out. You were very, very judicious in your choice of vocabulary in terms of what you were implying. I think I get your drift.
turns.zh: 我不会排除这种可能。你在措辞上非常谨慎，我明白你的言下之意。

turns.en: And all I would say that serious people who take this matter seriously are having serious discussions about the serious likelihood of that happening.
turns.zh: 我只想说，严肃的人在严肃地讨论这件事严肃发生的可能性。

turns.en: Let's move on to that other war that is going on. It's particularly interesting to me that it almost seemed scripted for Hollywood that President Trump was unusually vocal and publicly vocal in issuing a warning almost to President Zelensky saying, look, the world needs diesel right now.
turns.zh: 我们来说说另一场正在进行的战争。让我特别感兴趣的是，事情几乎像是给好莱坞写好的剧本：Trump 总统罕见地公开发声，几乎是在警告 Zelensky 总统说：听着，全世界现在都需要柴油。

turns.en: Go ahead and have your war with Russia, but do not hit their refineries because it's going to shock the global market. Don't do that. It was days later that Ukraine did exactly that almost seemingly in an intentional, I mean, the way I read it was an intentional act of defiance like, no, Mr. Trump, you're not going to tell us what to do.
turns.zh: 你要跟俄罗斯打你的仗可以，但不要打他们的炼厂，因为这会震动全球市场。不要这么做。几天之后，乌克兰做的恰恰就是这个，看起来几乎是——至少我读到的感觉是——一种故意的挑衅：不，Trump 先生，你休想指挥我们。

turns.en: Maybe I'm reading that wrong. Did you see it? No, I think that's a very valid way of reading it. All I can say is that there are different ways to interpret it, depending on whether you look at this first order, second order, third order, et cetera.
turns.zh: 也许我读错了。你怎么看？不，我觉得这是一种非常合理的解读。我只能说，根据你从第一层、第二层、第三层等等去看，会有不同的解读方式。

turns.en: And I'm not implying that the other views are correct. I'm just saying that you have to look at a matrix of potential outcomes and possibilities.
turns.zh: 我并不是说其他解读就一定对，我只是说你必须去看一个由潜在结果和可能性构成的矩阵。

turns.en: So one of them is that, yes, Trump says things and people just defy him now. That's not particularly good for the global security order. It's good if you don't like Trump, you know, which puts a smile on some people's face and a scowl on others, but it's not good in terms of global security.
turns.zh: 其中一种就是：没错，Trump 说话，人们就是公然违抗他。这对全球安全秩序并不是好事。如果你不喜欢 Trump，那可能挺爽——这会让一部分人偷笑，另一部分人皱眉——但从全球安全的角度看，这并不是好事。

turns.en: And it's certainly not good in terms of diesel prices for the global economy. That's one. The other one is if you think second, third order, that if that's going to happen, you are starting to see record diesel prices, not just in the US, which is a course where American voters are looking at it, but right the way around the world, you are seeing serious signs of political stress, economic stress, and even social unrest in some countries on
turns.zh: 从全球经济的柴油价格角度看，当然也不是好事。这是一层。另一层是，如果你从二阶、三阶去看，如果这种情况继续下去，你会看到柴油价格创出新高，不只是在美国——美国选民当然会盯着——而是全球各地；你会看到严重的政治压力、经济压力，甚至一些国家出现社会动荡，

turns.en: the back of that now. And the longer this goes on, the worse it's going to get. Now as an adjunct to that, and maybe we'll open that discussion in a second, you have had Republican politicians and now even Trump himself and Bessent investigating the idea of ceasing US diesel exports.
turns.zh: 这些都是由此引发的。而且这种情况拖得越久就越糟。作为补充——也许我们一会儿展开——你已经看到共和党政客，现在甚至 Trump 本人和 Bessent 都在研究停止美国柴油出口的想法。

turns.en: And before we unpack that, and how that may or may not play out, were that to happen, and again, this is purely hypothetical, were that to happen, what do you think the impact would be Russia, Ukraine, and Europe?
turns.zh: 在我们展开这个话题、讨论它可能怎么走之前——如果这真的发生，这纯粹是假设——如果真的发生，你觉得会对俄罗斯、乌克兰和欧洲产生什么影响？

turns.en: There are different ways to look at it, but one of them is that Europe, which is potentially in the firing line to not get as much diesel in that particular environment, would have to be the ones who clipped Zelensky's ear and say, we've told you not to hit Russian oil refineries.
turns.zh: 可以从不同角度看，其中一个角度是：欧洲——在这种环境下可能拿不到那么多柴油、正处在火力线上——就得去揪 Zelensky 的耳朵，说：我们告诉过你不要打俄罗斯的炼油厂。

turns.en: Didn't you listen to the man talking about Trump? Because they would be the ones who suffer more. So then that would actually force them to be tougher with Ukraine and actually get them to try and force some kind of settlement rather than an escalation, which seems more likely at the moment between Russia, Ukraine, and Europe behind Ukraine.
turns.zh: 你没听到 Trump 说的话吗？因为受损失更大的会是他们。这样一来反而会逼他们对乌克兰更强硬，真正推动某种和解，而不是像目前这样在俄罗斯、乌克兰和支持乌克兰的欧洲之间看起来更可能升级。

turns.en: So that's one very cynical second order way of looking at it. Equally, and the data on this are not conclusive, but some of the whispers that you hear and the stories that you hear from oil traders, don't rule out the fact that there's actually arbitrage happening and some refined products are still flowing from Europe to Russia itself.
turns.zh: 所以这是一种非常犬儒的二阶解读。同样——这方面的数据并不确定，但你从原油交易员那里听到的一些风声和故事——不要排除这样一种可能：其实存在套利，一些成品油仍在从欧洲流向俄罗斯本土。

turns.en: By that happening, you would then put pressure on them to stop doing that. So there are different ways to interpret it, but as is often the case when we're looking at geopolitics and the intersection of geopolitics and geo-economics, don't always fall for the first order Trump-related headline and just as an adjunct, one last point before we go back to the diesel thing, just a few months ago, for example, we had panic after panic
turns.zh: 如果真是这样，那你就会有筹码去施压让他们停下来。所以有多种解读方式。但就像我们讨论地缘政治以及地缘政治与地缘经济交叉时经常说的那样：不要一看到跟 Trump 有关的一阶标题就上头。作为补充，最后一点，在我们回到柴油话题之前——比如几个月前，欧洲一次次恐慌

turns.en: in Europe that Trump was going to invade Greenland. Serious people saying, well, there's a risk that will actually be a war with America and nine or 13 soldiers from Europe actually went to Greenland.
turns.zh: Trump 要入侵格陵兰。有严肃的人说：搞不好会跟美国真打一仗。结果欧洲只派了 9 个还是 13 个士兵去格陵兰。

turns.en: He's just signed that security agreement with Greenland and Denmark, which is pretty much everything that he wanted from the beginning. And so there's been an enormous climb down from the European side on that, despite the fact that all the first order headlines were doom, gloom, catastrophe and very much a simplistic way of looking at it.
turns.zh: 他刚刚跟格陵兰和丹麦签了那份安全协议，内容几乎就是他一开始想要的全部。所以在这一问题上欧洲一方作出了巨大的退让，尽管所有的一阶标题都是末日、悲观、灾难，是一种非常简化式的看法。

turns.en: I promise to come back to the diesel export policy in a minute, but before we talk about diesel, let's talk about diesel because I want to talk about just the global shortage aspect before we even get into US policy.
turns.zh: 我保证一会儿回到柴油出口政策，但在讨论柴油政策之前，我们先聊聊柴油本身——我想先谈谈全球短缺这一面，然后再进入美国政策。

turns.en: In the escalation of all this, a lot of us were really talking about blowout $200 crude oil prices. Our friend Dr. Anas Alhaji, who you mentioned earlier, was the voice of reason saying, guys, you're misreading it.
turns.zh: 在这轮升级当中，我们很多人其实在讨论原油价格飙到 200 美元。我们的朋友 Anas Alhajji 博士——你刚才提到过他——当时是那个理性的声音，他说：各位，你们读错了。

turns.en: Yes, there is a spike. It won't be in the benchmark products. There will be $200 oil prices. There have already been $200 oil prices in local markets, but it's not going to come to the benchmarks.
turns.zh: 是的，会出现价格尖峰，但不会发生在基准油种上。会有 200 美元的油价——本地市场其实已经出现过 200 美元的油价了，但不会传导到基准上。

turns.en: The same guy who was Mr. Voice of Reason is in the last couple of days post the Russian strike that I think took out something like 40% of Russian diesel refining capacity.
turns.zh: 同一位「理性之声」先生，在过去几天，也就是俄罗斯那次打击之后——我认为那次打击摧毁了俄罗斯大约 40% 的柴油炼化能力——

turns.en: Anas, who is the never escalate man, is saying, diesel is the crisis. He's tweeting all over the place. It seems like we really do have a very serious risk of this thing mushrooming.
turns.zh: Anas，这个从来不建议升级的人，现在到处发推说：柴油才是真正的危机。看起来我们真的面临着这件事迅速蔓延的严重风险。

turns.en: To what extent is that risk? I want to make sure we put it in perspective for people that when you run out of diesel fuel in a country, it means your farmers can't deliver food to people.
turns.zh: 这个风险到底有多大？我想帮大家把它放到语境里：一个国家如果没有柴油，就意味着农民没法把食物送到人们手里。

turns.en: It means that the rest of things, whether it's groceries or necessities, if the trucks can't drive down the road because they can't refuel, nothing gets anywhere.
turns.zh: 就意味着其他东西，不管是杂货还是生活必需品，如果卡车因为加不上油不能上路，什么都运不到任何地方。

turns.en: Diesel crisis could be a really big deal. It could lead to rationing and so forth. Are we headed to that extent of potentially a global diesel crisis, or is this just a bunch of propaganda that's been exaggerated on X?
turns.zh: 柴油危机可能是一件非常大的事，可能导致配给制等等。我们真的有可能走向一场全球柴油危机吗？还是这只是 X 上被夸大的一堆宣传？

turns.en: Well, first of all, I have to reiterate again, as a global strategist, I have to look across asset, cross geography, and frankly, cross disciplinary, but that doesn't make me an energy expert.
turns.zh: 首先，我要再重申一遍：作为一名全球策略师，我必须跨资产、跨地域、坦白说还要跨学科地看，但这并不意味着我就是能源专家。

turns.en: I speak to many of them, and our own energy expert at Rabobank, Joe DeLaura, who does a fantastic job on oil, he's deeply concerned. If you look at the supply demand, if you look at where inventories are, if you look at the fact that in most parts of the West, in particular, we haven't built a refinery for a very long time and have been busily closing them down, and if you look at the disruption happening
turns.zh: 我跟很多能源专家交流，我们 Rabobank 自己的能源专家 Joe DeLaura，在原油方面做得非常出色，他非常担忧。如果你看供需，看库存水平，看这样一个事实：西方大部分地区，尤其是很久没有新建炼厂了，反而在忙着关闭炼厂，再看

turns.en: in the Middle East, which is easing for the moment, but as I said, could come roaring back in again alongside what's happening to Russia, you can make a realistic prognosis that a genuine, really serious diesel crisis is possible, but at that point, I have to steer it back to something I said early on, and which I've said repeatedly in the past couple of weeks, and even the past couple of days to people, which is when we are looking
turns.zh: 中东正在发生的供应中断——目前有所缓和，但正如我说过，随时可能卷土重来，再叠加俄罗斯正在发生的事——你可以做出一个合理的判断：一场真正的、非常严重的柴油危机是有可能的。但说到这里，我必须把话头拉回到我一开始就说过、过去几周甚至过去几天反复跟大家讲的一点：当我们看

turns.en: at these things, the joke at the moment is if you're an interest rate trader or an FX trader at the moment, you have to be an oil trader. You've got to look at that to understand what bond yields are going to do, for example.
turns.zh: 这些东西的时候，圈子里现在的玩笑是：如果你现在是利率交易员或外汇交易员，你就得同时是原油交易员。你必须盯油，才能搞清楚比如债券收益率接下来会怎么走。

turns.en: Fair enough. I think that's a valid comment. For the oil traders, okay, they tend to be much more real politic because of the way the market is and the industry is.
turns.zh: 这也说得通，我觉得这个说法是成立的。对原油交易员来说，好，他们往往更加「现实政治」（realpolitik），因为这个市场和这个行业就是这样。

turns.en: You've got to understand global strategy. You've really got to understand who's more likely to win the war, who's more likely to escalate or de-escalate, who's bluffing, who isn't.
turns.zh: 你必须懂全球战略。你必须真正搞清楚谁更可能赢下这场战争，谁更可能升级或降级，谁在虚张声势，谁没有。

turns.en: That's a very, very different set of skills that you're having to bring and a very different set of lenses you're having to look through to determine this, and by the way, that goes all the way to central banks.
turns.zh: 这是一套非常非常不同的技能，你要透过一套非常不同的镜头来判断。顺便说一句，这也一路延伸到央行。

turns.en: If you want to talk about what the Fed's going to do, what's the ECB going to do, what's the Bank of England going to do. We can understand or try and guess what the reaction function is, but it's all a reaction to the geopolitics.
turns.zh: 如果你想讨论美联储要做什么、ECB（欧洲央行）要做什么、英国央行要做什么，我们可以理解或者猜测他们的反应函数，但所有的反应都是对地缘政治的反应。

turns.en: Steering back to that, you look at Russia, Ukraine, are we close to escalation or peace in our time? Between the two, if you're going to make it binary like that on a buy, sell basis, we're far closer to escalation than we are to peace in our time.
turns.zh: 把话题拉回来，你看俄罗斯、乌克兰：我们是接近升级还是接近「我们这代人的和平」？如果你要把它简化成二选一，从买入卖出的角度，我们距离升级远比距离「我们这代人的和平」更近。

turns.en: In the Middle East, are we closer to another escalation to try to get through to the other side of it than we are to, we're all friends and we're going to toast marshmallows around the fire, sing in Kumbaya.
turns.zh: 在中东，我们是更接近再一次升级、试图打到另一头，还是更接近「大家都是朋友，我们要围着篝火烤棉花糖、唱 Kumbaya」？

turns.en: We're far closer to an escalation. In fact, both of those wars are closer to a conflation and a conflagration, where we see that actually they are the same war, albeit being fought by slightly different people.
turns.zh: 我们距离升级要近得多。事实上，这两场战争都更接近融合成一场大火并——我们看到它们其实是同一场战争，只不过是由略微不同的人来打。

turns.en: On that basis, yes, the risk is there if we don't get the right geopolitical outcomes and the right reactions from policymakers or the diesel crisis, the risk.
turns.zh: 在这个基础上，是的，如果我们没有得到正确的地缘政治结果，没有得到政策制定者正确的反应，那么柴油危机的风险就在那里。

turns.en: Michael, I think you're really onto something about it being all the same conflict and the question that comes back to my mind that I just can't shake is, what possible motive could anyone who was influencing Zelensky have had in order to want to bring on a global diesel crisis or why would Zelensky, maybe Zelensky felt that his war wasn't getting enough attention and he needed to do something to draw attention to it.
turns.zh: Michael，我觉得你真的说到了点子上——这一切都是同一场冲突。我脑子里始终甩不掉的一个问题是：任何一个能影响 Zelensky 的人，怎么可能希望引发一场全球柴油危机？或者，为什么 Zelensky 会这么做？也许 Zelensky 觉得他的战争没有获得足够关注，他需要做点什么来把注意力拉回来。

turns.en: It seems to me that if Zelensky is the guy who just very, very flagrantly disobeyed Trump's direct order not to hit the diesel refineries, he took out something like 40% of their refining capacity.
turns.zh: 在我看来，如果 Zelensky 就是那个非常公然违抗 Trump 直接命令、不打柴油炼厂的人，他一举摧毁了大约 40% 的炼化能力——

turns.en: I may have that number wrong, folks. I got that off of X and I haven't verified it. But if he did that, and I mean, it seems like he would have pissed the whole world off and they're all going to blame him for escalating at the wrong time in a way that caused a diesel crisis that's affecting the safety of countries around the world.
turns.zh: 各位，这个数字我可能记错了，我是从 X 上看来的，还没核实。但如果他真的做了这件事，我是说，他好像会惹恼全世界，所有人都会怪他在错误的时机升级，引发了一场影响世界各国安全的柴油危机。

turns.en: He's not that stupid unless there's a bigger picture that I'm not seeing. I don't want to get into conspiracy theories because X, social media, is full of them and there are some fantastic ones and some fantastically awful ones out there.
turns.zh: 他没那么蠢，除非有一幅我看不到的更大图景。我不想陷入阴谋论，因为 X 这样的社交媒体上到处都是阴谋论，有些还挺精彩，也有些糟糕得让人叹为观止。

turns.en: And I think we can all admit it's fun to dabble in that from time to time just out of interest to hear what people are saying. That's not the world that I live in.
turns.zh: 我想我们都可以承认，偶尔出于好奇去听听大家说什么、玩玩这些阴谋论，是挺有意思的。但那不是我生活的世界。

turns.en: I live in the real world. But what I will tell you is in the real world, as I already said, the mainstream view that you're seeing from the mainstream press, and I mean the mainstream financial press as well about what's going on with a given story, Trump's going to invade Greenland, et cetera, et cetera, are very, very, very wrong most of the time.
turns.zh: 我生活在真实世界。但我可以告诉你，在真实世界里，就像我已经说过的那样，你在主流媒体——我说的也包括主流财经媒体——上看到的关于某条新闻、Trump 要入侵格陵兰等等的主流叙事，绝大多数时候都错得非常、非常、非常离谱。

turns.en: And they don't see that there is often, as I said, a second or a third order or a second or a third layer that's taking place. And historically, you only find out afterwards.
turns.zh: 他们看不到，就像我说的，事情往往还有第二层、第三层，还有第二个、第三个层次在同时展开。而在历史上，你只能事后才知道。

turns.en: I mean, let's go all the way back, for example. This is one that's well-recognized now. The Gulf of Tonkin incident with the Vietnam War, the nominal trigger that the US used to really escalate and get involved in the war, completely fake.
turns.zh: 我是说，我们甚至可以往回追溯。举个例子，这一点现在已经广为人知了：越南战争的「北部湾事件」（Gulf of Tonkin incident），美国用来真正升级、介入这场战争的名义导火索，完全是假的。

turns.en: So thunderstorm, as far as I'm aware, unless that's a conspiracy theory that I've fallen for at which point, I apologize to everybody. But you have false flags.
turns.zh: 据我所知就是一场所谓的「雷暴」，除非这也是我上当受骗的阴谋论之一——那样的话我向大家道歉。但你的确会有「假旗行动」（false flags）。

turns.en: You have multi-layered reasons for these things to be happening. And I do think there is some logic to Zelensky trying to keep the world's focus on this war.
turns.zh: 你会有多层次的原因在促成这些事情发生。我确实认为，Zelensky 试图让全世界的注意力留在这场战争上，是有一定逻辑的。

turns.en: Because frankly, the West gets bored really quickly and loses its focus really, really quickly. That doesn't mean that there can't be other motives out there.
turns.zh: 因为坦白说，西方很快就会觉得无聊，非常非常快就会失焦。这并不意味着不可能存在其他动机。

turns.en: And I very rarely avoid a topic, but I don't want to go too deep into all of them because they lead us to some places that we need another hour to discuss, just in terms of unpacking all of it.
turns.zh: 我很少回避话题，但我不想在这里把所有动机都展开，因为它们会把我们带到一些需要再多一个小时才能讨论清楚的地方。

turns.en: But I suspect that there is far more to this than we see above and beyond just trying to get attention. And one tell, just one tell on that, is apart from Trump, nobody else is angry with Zelensky.
turns.zh: 但我怀疑，除了单纯想吸引注意力之外，这件事背后还有很多我们看不到的东西。有一个信号——就一个信号——是：除了 Trump，没有其他人对 Zelensky 生气。

turns.en: So we have a global or a global diesel crisis. We have Europe suffering terribly, even though Europe is pro-Ukrainian. And yet all of this gets pinned again on Trump.
turns.zh: 所以我们有一场全球的柴油危机。欧洲苦不堪言，即便欧洲是亲乌克兰的。可所有这些又都被再次归咎到 Trump 头上。

turns.en: Now I'm not saying he's blameless in any way, shape or form. Clearly this war in the Middle East is a large, large part of it. But it's not as if the blame is being apportioned 70, 30 or 80, 20 or 50, 50.
turns.zh: 我并不是说他在任何方面、任何形式上都没有责任。显然，中东这场战争是其中很大很大的一部分。但你看，责任并不是按 70:30、80:20 或者 50:50 分配的。

turns.en: It's very clear where the mainstream narrative is going and it's unidirectional. Well, I think you said it best, Michael. On one hand, it would be irresponsible of us to try to venture into conspiracy theories and speculation about what is going on.
turns.zh: 主流叙事要往哪里走非常清楚，而且是单向的。嗯，Michael，我觉得你说得最好。一方面，如果我们试图去搞阴谋论和猜测，那就是不负责任。

turns.en: But boy, I have an overwhelmingly strong feeling that we're not seeing the whole picture yet and that there's more to this than meets the eye.
turns.zh: 但天哪，我有一种极其强烈的感觉：我们还没有看到全貌，这件事远比表面看到的要复杂。

turns.en: And I guess we'll just leave it there because I can't offer a credible explanation. I don't have any evidence, but this whole business of Trump makes a threat, then the very next thing that Zelensky does is defy it and then all the people around the world that ought to be pissed off at Zelensky aren't.
turns.zh: 我想我们就聊到这里吧，因为我给不出一个可信的解释。我没有证据。但整件事——Trump 发出威胁，紧接着 Zelensky 做的下一件事就是违抗它，然后全世界那些本该对 Zelensky 火大的人却都不火大——

turns.en: Something doesn't add up. But let's move on. We already talked about the diesel crisis. Now the Trump administration policy response proposal is, well, let's just put America first.
turns.zh: 有些地方说不通。但我们继续。我们已经谈过柴油危机。现在 Trump 政府的政策应对提案是：那就「美国优先」吧。

turns.en: And I shouldn't say it is Trump personally. I think it was someone else in the administration who actually escalated this idea of let's put America first and outlaw diesel exports from the United States.
turns.zh: 我不该说这是 Trump 个人的意思。我想是政府里的其他人把这个「美国优先、禁止美国柴油出口」的想法推上来的。

turns.en: And what they apparently believe is that will cause diesel prices to stay low in the United States even if they're high elsewhere. I don't know many people in the oil business who think that that's how the global market works.
turns.zh: 他们显然相信，这样能让美国的柴油价格保持低位，即便其他地方价格高企。我认识的行业里，没有多少人认为全球市场是这么运作的。

turns.en: But what do you think? I don't know anybody in the global oil business who thinks that's how the market works either. But I have one really important caveat to add to that.
turns.zh: 但你怎么看？我在全球石油行业里也不认识任何一个认为市场是这么运作的人。但我有一个非常重要的但书要加。

turns.en: And again, it's something that we've discussed in the past, which is this. I think you can agree, besides the fact that we have two major wars happening in the background, both of which look more likely to escalate than de-escalate.
turns.zh: 这也是我们过去讨论过的一点，是这样：我想你会同意，除了背景里有两场大战、两场看起来都更可能升级而不是降级之外——

turns.en: I think we're on agreement there. And we have a generalized trend, even though we have a Trump-sheet summit coming up imminently, we are still on a generalized trend towards tariffs, protectionism, decoupling, and fragmentation of portions of the global economy across various different sectors, particularly the US, China.
turns.zh: 我想我们在这点上是一致的——即便我们即将迎来一次 Trump-Xi 峰会，我们仍然处在一个总体趋势当中：走向关税、保护主义、脱钩，以及全球经济在不同板块、特别是美中之间的碎片化。

turns.en: Trump now increasingly talking about a trade war with China as well to try and protect his industry. We have those together. And yet because of the legacy structures that we have for the global energy market, it's still a one-world market.
turns.zh: Trump 现在也越来越多地谈论跟中国打贸易战，来保护本国产业。我们把这些放在一起看。然而，由于全球能源市场遗留下来的结构，它仍然是一个统一的世界市场。

turns.en: It's fabulously integrated across geography and across countries, regardless of politics, and it operates as a relatively efficient global system.
turns.zh: 它跨地域、跨国界高度一体化，不受政治影响，作为一个相对高效的全球系统在运作。

turns.en: Now, my hypothesis is this. Not how important energy is to everything. You were talking about diesel and how important that is in agriculture and industries, the lifeblood of both, and of logistics, right?

turns.zh: 这大致——我说得非常不客气、非常粗糙——就是我认为我们正在走向的方向。如果真是这样，那么所有对当前系统运作方式比我懂一千倍的能源专家，只要他们的所有观点都建立在「这是一个一体化的全球系统、并且会继续如此」的假设上，他们就都错了。因为实际上美国可以用经济治国术（economic statecraft），比如《国防生产法》（Defense Production Act），来命令炼厂

turns.zh: 该怎么做。它可以动用《国防生产法》下令建设更多的柴油储备设施，可以下令把柴油存在船上当浮动储备，可以按地区储存。它可以远远比现在这样更深地介入能源，把它当作国家安全领域。所以如果我们把它当成一个商业部门来讨论，每个细分环节都想在资本主义下作为一个独立业务赚自己的回报，
